bills.title: Equitable access to credit
bills.description: Creating the Washington equitable access to credit act.

bills.title: Emergency comm. sales tax
bills.description: Concerning sales and use tax for emergency communication systems and facilities.

bills.title: Main street program
bills.description: Modifying the Washington main street program tax incentive to respond to the economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic.

bills.title: Auto dealers/cash incentives
bills.description: Providing that qualified dealer cash incentives paid to auto dealers are bona fide discounts for purposes of the business and occupation tax.

bills.title: Lodging-related assessments
bills.description: Concerning lodging-related assessments under chapter 35.87A RCW.

bills.title: Affordable housing/REET
bills.description: Exempting a sale or transfer of real property for affordable housing to a nonprofit entity, housing authority, public corporation, county, or municipal corporation from the real estate excise tax.

bills.title: Health benefit ex./B&O tax
bills.description: Ensuring the ongoing sustainability and vitality of the Washington health benefit exchange by eliminating the expiration date of its business and occupation tax exemption.

bills.title: Community solar projects
bills.description: Expanding equitable access to the benefits of renewable energy through community solar projects.

bills.title: Data centers tax preference
bills.description: Providing a tax preference for rural and nonrural data centers.

bills.title: Motion picture program
bills.description: Updating and expanding the motion picture competitiveness program.

bills.title: BPA ratepayer assist/B&O tax
bills.description: Extending the business and occupation tax exemption for amounts received as credits against contracts with or funds provided by the Bonneville power administration and used for low-income ratepayer assistance and weatherization.

bills.title: Capital gains tax
bills.description: Enacting an excise tax on gains from the sale or exchange of certain capital assets. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Investing in Washington families and creating a more progressive tax system in Washington by enacting an excise tax on the sale or exchange of certain capital assets. )

bills.title: Salmon recovery grants/tax
bills.description: Concerning the taxation of salmon recovery grants by updating the state business and occupation tax deduction for these grants, creating a sales and use tax exemption for grant proceeds received by recipients of these grants, and clarifying the sales and use tax obligations for goods and services purchased by recipients of these grants.

bills.title: Farmworker housing/tax
bills.description: Expanding the sales and use tax exemption for farmworker housing.

bills.title: B&O tax credits
bills.description: Providing substantial and permanent tax relief for small businesses to mitigate structural deficiencies in Washington's business and occupation tax and lessen long-term negative economic consequences of the pandemic that have disproportionately impacted small businesses.

notes: SHB 1155 is counted as a tax increase without a state revenue estimate because it expands local taxing authority: it lets large counties impose the emergency communications sales tax without a public vote.
HB 1495, a B&O deduction for auto dealers, passed both chambers and was vetoed; the veto counts as the governor's no on a tax cut.

Two bills that paired a new tax break with offsetting changes (SSB 5799 and ESB 5901) and the 2022 transportation package (ESSB 5974, whose tax-law changes only move existing sales tax between accounts) are not counted.
Only taxes in Titles 82 and 84 of state law are counted, so the WA Cares long-term-care premium (Title 50B) and Move Ahead Washington's vehicle fees (Title 46) are not part of this record.
